test_title: PYST 10: SSC MTS - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 7 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: The profit earned on selling a bike for ₹ 68,250 is the same as the loss incurred on selling the bike for ₹ 47,250. Find the cost price of the bike.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the profit earned on selling an article is exactly equal to the loss incurred, the Cost Price (CP) is simply the average of the two selling prices.

CP = (SP₁ + SP₂) ÷ 2

CP = (68250 + 47250) ÷ 2

CP = 115500 ÷ 2 = 57750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 57,750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price with profit (SP₁) = ₹ 68,250

Selling Price with loss (SP₂) = ₹ 47,250

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4583e1dea2de780f3534e02f43013abc191003ff65c221c28fff763d0b860f72.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Loss = CP − SP

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = Loss

⇒ 68250 − CP = CP − 47250

⇒ CP + CP = 68250 + 47250

⇒ 2 × CP = 115500

⇒ CP = 115500 ÷ 2

⇒ CP = 57750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 57,750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

When an article is sold at a gain, SP > CP. The difference is Profit = SP − CP. When it is sold at a loss, CP > SP. The difference is Loss = CP − SP.

When Profit equals Loss

If the profit made by selling an article at SP₁ is exactly equal to the loss incurred by selling it at SP₂, then the Cost Price (CP) is the arithmetic mean of the two selling prices. CP = (SP₁ + SP₂) ÷ 2.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
